KeyPassages: 1 Samuel 14:11; 2 Kings 12:9; Job 30:6; Song of Solomon 5:4
BiblicalUsage: A hole is a hiding place and a poor man's home: the Philistines watch the Hebrews creep out of their holes, Job's outcasts live in the clefts of the rocks, and a priest bores a hole in a chest for the temple money. The beloved puts her hand through the hole of the door in the Song, and the same small opening becomes a place of longing.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that holes in Scripture mark the low places — fear, poverty, and hiding — and also the small openings through which love and generosity enter. God sees the people in the holes, and He does not leave them there. I believe that is why the chest with a hole in its lid matters: even a small opening can carry the gifts of a whole people.
